# Effect: distortion

Distortion modelled on a guitar amp (mid push before two clipping stages, cabinet with presence peak): overdrive, distortion, fuzz or wavefolding; loudness is compensated automatically, so more drive means more grit, not more volume.

**Where to put it**: On a guitar, bass, organ or synth track for rock / metal / grunge; lightly (overdrive, drive 6-12) on drums or a bus for grit. For a rock guitar: yinse.pluck.electric_guitar + { "mode": "distortion", "drive_db": 24, "cabinet": "guitar" }; play power chords (root + fifth), not full triads, since distortion turns thirds muddy.

Latest parameters: `muser effects distortion` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `distortion` | `overdrive` / `distortion` / `fuzz` / `fold` | overdrive: soft, asymmetric tube-like clipping; distortion: smooth saturation, rock / metal; fuzz: hard clipping, buzzy; fold: wavefolding, metallic synth sounds |
| `cabinet` | `none` | `none` / `guitar` / `bass` | Speaker cabinet simulation after the distortion: guitar: a low bump, a scooped low-mid, a presence peak near 3 kHz and a steep roll-off above ~6.5 kHz; bass keeps the lows and rolls off above ~3 kHz |
| `drive_db` | 18 | 0 – 48 dB | Drive. 6-12 crunch; 18-30 rock / metal; 36+ fuzz-like saturation |
| `tone_hz` | 8000 | 500 – 12000 Hz | Low-pass after the distortion: lower is darker, higher adds fizz |
| `low_cut_hz` | 100 | 20 – 1000 Hz | High-pass before the distortion so the lows don't turn to mud; 100-200 for tight metal rhythm, 40 for bass |
| `output_db` | 0 | -24 – 12 dB | Output level after the automatic loudness compensation |
| `mix` | 1 | 0 – 1 | Dry/wet mix; around 0.5 on bass keeps the clean low end under the grit |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "distortion", "mode": "distortion", "drive_db": 24, "cabinet": "guitar" }
```

## Scenario presets

- Crunch rhythm guitar (yinse.pluck.electric_guitar)

  ```json
  {"type": "distortion", "mode": "overdrive", "drive_db": 12, "cabinet": "guitar"}
  ```

- Rock / metal guitar (power chords)

  ```json
  {"type": "distortion", "mode": "distortion", "drive_db": 28, "low_cut_hz": 120, "tone_hz": 4000, "cabinet": "guitar"}
  ```

- Fuzz lead

  ```json
  {"type": "distortion", "mode": "fuzz", "drive_db": 30, "tone_hz": 3500, "cabinet": "guitar"}
  ```

- Gritty bass (clean lows kept)

  ```json
  {"type": "distortion", "mode": "overdrive", "drive_db": 18, "low_cut_hz": 40, "cabinet": "bass", "mix": 0.5}
  ```

- Dirty drum bus

  ```json
  {"type": "distortion", "mode": "overdrive", "drive_db": 8, "tone_hz": 9000, "mix": 0.4}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Loudness is compensated automatically: raising drive_db adds grit, not volume; set the level with gain_db / output_db as usual.
- Distorted guitars want power chords (root + fifth, maybe the octave); full triads with thirds turn muddy under heavy drive.
- No added latency, so it can be added mid-way in a live session (`effects_add`).
- For a metal rhythm: low_cut_hz 120-200 keeps the palm-muted chugs tight; double the part on a second track panned to the other side.
